name: Colombia
genZNote: Colombia is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific and the Caribbean — and after decades defined by internal armed conflict, its 2016 peace agreement with the FARC became one of the most closely studied peace processes in modern history.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in the northwest of South America, uniquely positioned with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
The Andes Mountains split into three ranges within Colombia, creating dramatic terrain alongside Amazon rainforest in the south and Caribbean coastal plains in the north.
One of the most biodiverse countries in the world relative to its size, home to an extraordinary range of ecosystems from coast to rainforest to high-altitude páramo grasslands.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Spanish is the official language; the culture blends Indigenous, Spanish colonial, and African influences, particularly along its Caribbean and Pacific coasts.
Globally influential in literature through Nobel laureate Gabriel García Márquez, a pioneer of the 'magical realism' literary genre.
Renowned for cumbia and vallenato music traditions, and as a major centre of Latin American visual art (Fernando Botero).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A unitary presidential republic with a President as head of state and government, and a bicameral Congress.
Experienced decades of internal armed conflict involving government forces, paramilitary groups, and guerrilla organisations (notably the FARC), significantly shaping modern national history.
Signed a landmark 2016 peace agreement with the FARC guerrilla group, ending over 50 years of armed conflict, a widely studied global peace process.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant regional hub for biodiversity research given its position as one of the world's most biodiverse nations.
Growing pharmaceutical manufacturing and medical tourism sector, particularly for cosmetic and dental procedures.
Strong agricultural science base supporting its position as a leading global coffee producer, with protected-origin certification for Colombian coffee.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: An OECD member since 2020, reflecting significant recent economic and institutional development.
A close US security and trade partner, historically tied to counter-narcotics cooperation given the country's role in global cocaine production.
A founding member of the Pacific Alliance trade bloc alongside Chile, Mexico, and Peru.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Colombia maintain growing relations, with cooperation expanding in pharmaceuticals, IT services, and agricultural technology.
Colombia is an important source of coffee and emeralds, while trade in Indian pharmaceuticals and vehicles to Colombia has been growing.
Both countries have engaged in growing cultural exchange and periodic high-level diplomatic visits in recent years.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A major global coffee producer and exporter, alongside significant oil, coal, and emerald production.
An OECD member with a growing, diversifying economy strong in flowers (a major global cut-flower exporter), textiles, and services.
Historically associated with cocaine production, an issue central to decades of internal conflict and US counter-narcotics cooperation.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: The 2016 peace agreement ending over 50 years of armed conflict with the FARC.
World-renowned coffee production and export.
Gabriel García Márquez and the 'magical realism' literary tradition.
Being one of the most biodiverse countries in the world.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Colombian Peso (COP).
A major coffee producer and exporter, alongside significant oil, coal, and flower exports.
One of the fastest-growing economies in Latin America in recent decades.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: One of the most biodiverse countries on Earth, home to a share of the Amazon Rainforest and unique páramo highland ecosystems.
The Coffee Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Part of Spanish colonial rule until independence in 1819 under Simón Bolívar.
Experienced decades of internal armed conflict involving guerrilla groups (notably FARC), which signed a landmark peace agreement with the government in 2016.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1991 Constitution modernized the country's governance framework and expanded citizens' rights.
The 2016 peace accord with FARC marked a major turning point after over five decades of conflict.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football and cycling are hugely popular, with Colombian cyclists winning major international races including the Tour de France.
Nobel laureate author Gabriel García Márquez, a pioneer of magical realism, is globally celebrated.
Cartagena's walled colonial city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, OECD, and the Pacific Alliance.
A close security and trade partner of the United States in Latin America.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Colombia is a unitary presidential republic in northwestern South America with coasts on both the Pacific and Caribbean, known for its 2016 FARC peace agreement, coffee, and biodiversity.
keyFacts: 2016 peace agreement ended over 50 years of armed conflict with the FARC.
OECD member since 2020; major global coffee producer.
commonConfusion: Colombia is the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea — a distinctive geographic fact worth remembering.

highYieldFacts: Colombia: unitary presidential republic, capital Bogotá, coasts on both Pacific and Caribbean.
2016 peace agreement with FARC ended 50+ years of conflict; OECD member since 2020.
India-Colombia: growing trade in coffee, emeralds, pharmaceuticals; expanding diplomatic engagement.
commonTraps: Assuming Colombia has only a Caribbean coast — it also has a significant Pacific coastline.
Confusing the FARC peace agreement (2016) with the broader, longer history of Colombia's internal conflict.
mustRemember: Colombia: dual-coast nation, 2016 FARC peace deal, OECD member, top coffee exporter, growing India trade partner.
